rows.49:08a8:
Wait a moment.
If I'm telling the fourth story, there's no need to go all the way back to the newspaper club.
The story I meant to tell is about this cherry tree, too.
...My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
I must say, my heart skipped a beat when Fukuzawa started on a story about the cherry tree for the third one.
I couldn't believe that a first-year like you would know a story about this cherry tree.
After all, this story was a legend known only to a very select few.
...But I'm glad.
Glad that Fukuzawa's story was a lie.
Wherever did you hear that story about this cherry tree?
Some of it may well be accurate, but how on earth did you hear it, to come up with a fabrication like that?
Perhaps you have a gift for writing fiction, Fukuzawa.
Or are you simply a swindler?
...Please don't be angry with me.
I'm only telling the truth.
This place was a dumping ground for corpses during the war, you say?
This cherry tree was forced to watch horrifying sights, over and over, you say?
During the war, they threw living people away along with the dead?
That is ridiculous beyond words.
Besides, even if it were true, there are mountains of sights far more horrifying than that.{p}
rows.49:0cb0:
After all, they say this cherry tree is more than a thousand years old.
That much, I'll grant.
This area, you see, is famous for a great battle fought here in the Warring States period.
Have you studied your history?
Do you know what people with hardly any food ate to stay alive in the Warring States period?
...I'd rather not say it myself.
And do you know what kind of life they were forced to lead?
Stripping the armor and helmets off dead warlords and trading them for a pittance, peeling the scalps off heads and selling the hair, hunting down defeated samurai who had survived and ganging up to beat them...
Was all of that just a dream, I wonder?
Those heaps upon heaps of corpses back then must have given this cherry tree all the nourishment it needed to grow, don't you think?{p}
rows.49:0f28:
Heh heh...
If that were how it worked, every tree in Japan would have to be cursed.
No one could ever go cherry-blossom viewing.
Someone would have to die every time anyone set foot in a forest.{p}
rows.49:0fd8:
It's true that this cherry tree is steeped in a grudge.
Many grudges, in fact.
But they don't belong to the soldiers who died in the war, nor to the warlords who died in the Warring States period.
It's something else...
They're grudges born of the fierce, wicked attachment to this world of people who lived perfectly ordinary lives.
{a}{f:|}?
What you saw a little while ago was that grudge.
Not the soldiers who died in the war.
Now I'll tell you the truth.
The story of the real grudge that has taken hold of this cherry tree.
In return, will you make me a promise?
No matter what happens, you won't move from this spot until my story is over.
And you will never, ever scream.
Understood?{p}Can you promise me that?
rows.49:1274:
I'm so glad you promised me.
Well then, I'll begin.{p}
rows.49:12c0:
Everyone, would you look at that branch up high?
You can see one thick branch stretching out there, can't you?
That one, you see, is just right for hanging yourself.
Do you know what else this cherry tree is called?
It's called the 'Hanging Cherry.'{p}Do you know why?
rows.49:13b0: Someone hanged themselves from that branch
rows.49:13cc: There's a rumor that if you hang yourself from that branch, you go to heaven
rows.49:1470:
It's true that, in the past, quite a few people have hanged themselves from this cherry tree.
But not one of them died of their own free will.
They are chosen by the cherry tree.
You think I'm lying, don't you?
I'm not.
This cherry tree, you see, chooses one sacrifice every year.
Of its own will.
Of course, I doubt anyone has ever heard that someone hangs themselves from this tree every year.
{a}{f:|}, you and Fukuzawa are only first-years, so it's natural that you wouldn't know, but...
Besides, even if the school tried to hide a rumor like that, it couldn't.
It would be bound to spread.
A school where, every single year without fail, someone hangs themselves from the cherry tree... imagine that.
Creepy, isn't it?{p}
rows.49:1698: If you'd known about a rumor like that, you wouldn't have come to this school, would you?
rows.49:16e0: That has nothing to do with it
rows.49:1730:
Strange, isn't it?
Do you know why?
It's because the cherry tree buries the people who became its sacrifices beneath itself, all on its own.
That's why the bodies are never found.
Even so, the fact that someone has gone missing would remain, wouldn't it?
And yet no one ever finds out.
No one is surprised.
Not the teachers, not their friends, not their families: not a single person worries.
Why do you think that is?
The very existence of the sacrifice vanishes from everyone's minds.
In other words, for some reason, the person's whole past, every fact of the life they lived, is completely erased.{p}
rows.49:18f8:
Heh heh...
It becomes as though they never existed in the first place.
That's why no one notices.
That's why no one worries.{p}
rows.49:1974:
After all, no one knows anything about such a person.
Now, don't you want to know why the cherry tree needs sacrifices?{p}Aren't you interested, {a}{f:|}?
rows.49:1a84:
I despise liars.
I like honest people.
This cherry tree, you see, used to be a meeting place for couples.
This was decades ago now.{p}
rows.49:1bb0:
And it was said that a couple who kissed beneath this cherry tree and swore their love to each other would be bound together forever.
Back then, it didn't yet have such a hateful nickname as the Hanging Cherry.
It was a symbol of happiness that bound two lovers together.
At that time, there was a couple named Kunio Hirooka and Hatsuko Orihara.
They, too, believed in the legend of the cherry tree, and dreamed that someday they would kiss beneath it and be bound by eternal love.
But you know, legends like that aren't made only of happy stories.
There was a dark side, too.{p}
rows.49:1e94:
It's cleverly made, isn't it?
If eternal love came that easily, the legend would lose all its value.
That's why you hardly ever heard of a couple who had put the legend to the test, not even as a rumor.
Perhaps there were actually many of them.
Everyone was so pure that they were too shy to talk about it, and if they did talk and then broke up, they'd be a real laughingstock, wouldn't they?
Secrets like that, you see, were kept between the two of them alone.
So Hirooka and Orihara told no one either, and waited for the time to come.{p}
rows.49:2070:
Back then, making that kind of confession was the man's job.
These days so many men are spineless that the women seem to be the strong ones.
Around the time the cherry blossoms bloomed, Hirooka finally made up his mind.
He would perform the legendary ritual beneath the cherry tree in full bloom.
"...Orihara. If you don't mind, would you come with me, just the two of us, under those cherry blossoms?"
You understand what it meant when he said the two of them would go there, don't you?
Orihara blushed and gave a small nod.
How happy Hirooka was at that moment...
I can feel it as if it were in the palm of my hand.
And so he asked her.
"When would be good for you?"{p}What do you think Orihara answered?
rows.49:22ac: On the night of the next full moon
rows.49:22cc: I'll leave it up to you
rows.49:22dc:
"On the night of the next full moon. I think that's just when the cherry blossoms will be in full bloom. Then..."
The two held hands and gazed into each other's eyes.
No more words were needed.
Though anyone who has never been in love wouldn't understand.
Do you understand, I wonder?
...And so, at last, the night of the full moon arrived.
As the day drew closer and closer, their hearts pounded and fluttered.
On the day itself, knowing that tonight was the night, they were so shy that whenever their eyes met during the day, they couldn't help looking away.{p}
rows.49:2490:
At ten o'clock on the night of the full moon, the two met at the school's back gate.
It was a quiet night, without a soul around.
Of course, both of them had sneaked out of their homes.
If they'd told their families the truth, they would never have been allowed to go.
"Have you been waiting long?"
"No, I just got here."
Though each was sure the other would come, they had both been uneasy until they reached the back gate.
When they spotted each other, they ran to each other, neither one first, and took each other's hands.
And they nodded together.
It was a signal to confirm their resolve.{p}
rows.49:267c:
Then they passed alongside the old school building in the night and headed for that cherry tree.
The two of them could clearly feel their clasped hands growing damp with sweat.
However hard they tried not to notice, they could plainly hear their own hearts beating.
And even each other's.{p}
rows.49:2840:
Can you believe it? Someone had come to the cherry tree before them.
And at the very moment they were kissing, no less.
If the legend was true, misfortune would now fall upon that couple.
"Ah!"
And before they could stop themselves, they cried out.{p}
rows.49:2908:
The pair nestled together, hidden in the cherry tree's silhouette, broke off their kiss in surprise.
And they looked around.
Hirooka and Orihara squeezed each other's hands tight.
At this rate, they would be found.{p}What do you think the two of them did?
rows.49:29e8: They stepped out to explain what had happened
rows.49:2a14:
"Let's run!"
Hirooka grabbed her hand and broke into a run on the spot.
"Wait! Please, wait!"
A man's voice called out behind them.
But they didn't turn around.
It was a mournful voice, one that seemed to drape itself over their backs.
But the two of them were too frightened to look back.{p}
rows.49:2b1c:
And before they knew it, they had reached a nearby park.
"...What do we do?"
Orihara looked as if she might burst into tears at any moment.
Those people might hate them for this.
It had only been moonlight, but perhaps they had even seen their faces.
Thinking about it, she was so frightened that her tears overflowed and wouldn't stop.{p}What do you think Hirooka said to her then?
rows.49:2c70: Let's find them tomorrow and apologize
rows.49:2c8c: It's not our fault, so don't let it bother you
rows.49:2cb4: Let's keep this a secret between the two of us and say nothing
rows.49:2cdc:
"I couldn't see their faces. Could you, Orihara?"
Hirooka asked anxiously.
She only shook her head quietly.
At that, he made his decision.
He would keep quiet.
"Let's keep this a secret between just the two of us. That way, they're sure to accept that they were mistaken about seeing us.
And then they won't have to suffer any misfortune, will they?"
By saying so, Hirooka convinced himself as well.
In fact, perhaps that really was the best thing.
Orihara, too, decided to go along with Hirooka.
And so the two of them came to share a secret.
Having a secret of your own, just between two people, is important, you know.
When a man and a woman share a secret, their relationship moves forward quickly.
Perhaps the legend of the cherry tree was born from that very idea in the first place.
And then they parted, promising that tomorrow night, without fail, they would confirm their love once more.{p}
rows.49:3014:
By now, their eyes showed that they trusted each other completely.
Perhaps seeing another couple's kiss had, if anything, deepened the bond between them.
And it seemed that things would go well for the two of them.
But...{p}
rows.49:30f0:
The next day, a young man and woman were found hanged from the cherry tree, dead.
There was no suicide note.
They had died tied to each other with rope, so that their bodies wouldn't come apart.
Still in each other's arms.
Hirooka thought to himself.
The ones who had died must surely be the couple the two of them had seen.
They must have despaired that misfortune would come because their kiss had been seen, and turned to thoughts of suicide.
If they couldn't be together in this world, they would find happiness in heaven: that was what they had vowed.
Is that hard for you to believe?
Do you think it's ridiculous to die over something like that?
But you know, people in the old days took love very seriously.
Heh heh heh... though you may not understand that.
Orihara felt just the same way Hirooka did.{p}
rows.49:33a4: That night, the two of them met at the same time and in the same place as the night before.{p}
rows.49:33ec:
Even so, they found it hard to go to the cherry tree.
As for carrying out that legend, they were in no mood for anything of the kind.
Still, when they thought of the two who had died believing they'd been seen, they couldn't bear to be alone.
"...It's my fault. Because I ran away that time, they died. ...If I'd explained what happened then, those two might not have had to die."
Head bowed, Hirooka spoke weakly.
Orihara just cried in silence.
To be honest, the two of them had no idea what they should do from then on.
It was then.{p}
rows.49:3604:
Suddenly, a voice called out to the two of them.
Not a voice they could clearly hear with their ears, but one that called directly inside their heads.
At first they were startled, thinking someone somewhere was watching them.
But they couldn't sense anyone there.
And then, this time, they heard it clearly.{p}
rows.49:3708:
"You two killed them."
That was what the voice said, full of resentment.
Both of them were trembling so hard in the legs that they couldn't move.
The voice pressed on, as if to drive the point home.
"Because you saw them, two young lives were lost. If you had not had such wicked thoughts, time would have flowed on in peace. If you truly feel responsible, then let us see you take that so-called responsibility."
The voice was overbearing.
A heavy, oppressive voice without a shred of kindness in it.
The two hung their heads and fell silent.
The voice was demanding that they take responsibility.{p}What would you say?
rows.49:3928: There's no need to take responsibility
rows.49:3940: I don't want to talk to the likes of you
rows.49:395c:
I see.
You're surprisingly innocent, aren't you?
The two of them gave that answer, too.
Their consciences must have been tormenting them terribly.
"...It's true, I'm the one to blame. If I can, I want to take responsibility. ...What should I do?"
That was the answer Hirooka gave.
The voice that replied sounded pleased.{p}

notes: Speaker: Akemi Iwashita throughout (introduces herself in 08a8), telling the fourth story at the cherry tree; 08a8 lines 7-14 address Fukuzawa directly ('a first-year like you').
49:1408 follows only the 'I don't know' choice; rendered 'I see. / I thought as much.' to fit that answer.
49:2840: who cries out 'Ah!' is unstated (one or both of Hirooka/Orihara); kept as 'they'.
49:1974: moved {a}{f:|} to the end of the question for natural English; codes unchanged.
